section: State legislature - Assembly and Legislative Council; creation and abolition of the Council (Article 169)
subsections: Speaker of the Legislative Assembly - powers, casting vote, Money Bill, resignation, vacating
Article 169 - resolution majority, Parliament's role, Governor's role

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding vacation of the office of the Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly:
1. The Speaker ceases to hold office if he or she ceases to be a member of the Assembly.
2. The Speaker may resign by addressing the resignation to the Deputy Speaker.
3. The Speaker can be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Assembly after fourteen days' notice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements correctly state the grounds and procedure for vacating the Speaker's office under Article 179.
accepted.tq: Check each procedural condition separately, especially the notice period and required majority.
accepted.sec: Speaker of the Legislative Assembly - powers, casting vote, Money Bill, resignation, vacating  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A resolution for the removal of the Speaker is under consideration in the Legislative Assembly. Which one of the following is correct?
o: The Speaker presides and has only a casting vote
The Speaker does not preside, but may speak and vote in the first instance
The Speaker must leave the House and cannot participate in the proceedings
The Speaker cannot speak but may vote in the second instance
accepted.x: Under Article 181, the Speaker does not preside while a resolution for removal is under consideration, but may speak and vote in the first instance.
accepted.tq: Apply the special procedural exception to the presiding officer's normal powers.
accepted.sec: Speaker of the Legislative Assembly - powers, casting vote, Money Bill, resignation, vacating  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a power or function of the Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly?
o: Approving the creation of a Legislative Council in the State
Giving the final decision on whether a Bill is a Money Bill
Deciding disqualification under the Tenth Schedule, subject to judicial review
Adjourning or suspending the House in case of lack of quorum
accepted.x: The Speaker performs the first three functions. Creation or abolition of a Legislative Council involves an Assembly resolution followed by parliamentary law; it is not approved by the Speaker.
accepted.tq: Find the option assigning a constitutional function to the wrong authority.
accepted.sec: Speaker of the Legislative Assembly - powers, casting vote, Money Bill, resignation, vacating  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly ordinarily exercises a casting vote when:
o: The House lacks the required quorum
A Bill is introduced for the first time
The Governor returns a Bill for reconsideration
There is equality of votes on a question before the House
accepted.x: Under Article 189, the Speaker does not vote in the first instance but exercises a casting vote in the event of an equality of votes.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the ordinary vote from the deciding or casting vote.
accepted.sec: Speaker of the Legislative Assembly - powers, casting vote, Money Bill, resignation, vacating  [APPSC]

accepted.s: After the dissolution of a State Legislative Assembly, the Speaker continues in office until:
o: The Council of Ministers recommends termination of the office
Just before the first meeting of the newly elected Assembly
The Governor appoints a new Speaker
The date on which the election results are declared
accepted.x: The Speaker continues after dissolution until immediately before the first meeting of the new Assembly.
accepted.tq: Watch the precise end-point in tenure questions rather than the general duration.
accepted.sec: Speaker of the Legislative Assembly - powers, casting vote, Money Bill, resignation, vacating  [APPSC]

accepted.s: When the office of the Speaker is vacant or the Speaker is absent, the Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly:
o: Acts with the full powers of the Speaker
Can only conduct voting on Money Bills
Requires prior permission of the Governor to preside
Is replaced by the Chairman of the Legislative Council
accepted.x: The Deputy Speaker acts with the full powers of the Speaker when the office is vacant or the Speaker is absent.
accepted.tq: Ask which officer legally substitutes for the principal presiding officer.
accepted.sec: Speaker of the Legislative Assembly - powers, casting vote, Money Bill, resignation, vacating  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 168 — Constitution of State Legislatures
Article 172 — Qualifications of members
Article 174 — Composition of the Legislative Council
Article 208 — Financial procedure and Annual Financial Statement
accepted.x: Article 168 deals with the constitution of State Legislatures. Article 172 concerns duration, Article 174 concerns sessions, and Article 208 concerns rules of procedure.
accepted.tq: Use article-number anchors and reject swapped constitutional subjects.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below.

List-I (Article)
 a. 169
 b. 173
 c. 194
 d. 202

List-II (Subject)
 i. Qualifications for membership
 ii. Powers and privileges of State Legislatures
 iii. Creation or abolition of Legislative Councils
 iv. Annual Financial Statement
o: a–iii, b–i, c–ii, d–iv
a–ii, b–iii, c–iv, d–i
a–iv, b–ii, c–i, d–iii
a–i, b–iv, c–iii, d–ii
accepted.x: Article 169 concerns Legislative Councils, Article 173 qualifications, Article 194 privileges, and Article 202 the Annual Financial Statement.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure article-subject pair and eliminate codes containing a mismatch.

accepted.s: Which Article provides for the duration of a State Legislative Assembly?
o: Article 187
Article 176
Article 169
Article 172
accepted.x: Article 172 deals with the duration of State Legislatures; the normal duration of the Legislative Assembly is five years unless sooner dissolved.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between adjacent constitutional provisions by their specific subject.

accepted.s:
With reference to Articles 174 to 176, consider the following statements:
1. Article 174 deals with sessions, prorogation and dissolution of the State Legislature.
2. Article 175 deals with the Governor's right to address and send messages to the House or Houses.
3. Article 176 deals with the Governor's special address.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Articles 174, 175 and 176 respectively concern sessions and dissolution, the Governor's address and messages, and the special address.
accepted.tq: Read a sequence of neighbouring articles together instead of treating one article in isolation.

accepted.s: The interval between the last sitting in one session of a State Legislature and the first sitting in the next session cannot exceed:
o: Six months
Three months
Four months
One year
accepted.x: Article 174 requires that not more than six months intervene between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next.
accepted.tq: Test the constitutional time limit directly and distinguish it from other legislative periods.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 210 — Language to be used in the Legislature
Article 187 — Secretariat of the State Legislature
Article 194 — Powers and privileges of State Legislatures
Article 212 — Annual Financial Statement
accepted.x: Article 212 concerns the exclusion of judicial inquiry into legislative proceedings. The Annual Financial Statement is dealt with under Article 202.
accepted.tq: Locate the article-subject swap among otherwise familiar constitutional provisions.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the State Legislature is correct?
1. Each House may make rules for regulating its procedure and conduct of business.
2. Courts cannot inquire into the proceedings of the Legislature merely on the ground of procedural irregularity.
3. Conduct of a High Court judge in the discharge of duties cannot be discussed in the State Legislature.
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Articles 208, 212 and 211 respectively support the three statements.
accepted.tq: Combine related constitutional safeguards and identify the option containing all applicable provisions.

accepted.s: The constitutional provision that no person can simultaneously be a member of both Houses of the Legislature of a State is contained in:
o: Article 187
Article 178
Article 190
Article 194
accepted.x: Article 190 provides, among other matters concerning vacation of seats, that a person cannot be a member of both Houses of a State Legislature at the same time.
accepted.tq: Match the specific membership restriction with its constitutional article.

accepted.s: The normal order of proceedings at the beginning of a session of a State Legislative Assembly, as indicated for the State Legislature, is:
o: Voting on demands, Governor's address, general discussion
Governor's address, general discussion, voting on demands
General discussion, voting on demands, Governor's address
Governor's address, voting on demands, general discussion
accepted.x: The indicated order is the Governor's address, followed by general discussion and then voting on demands in the Assembly.
accepted.tq: Arrange the stages in the stated procedural sequence, not by constitutional article number.

accepted.s: Under Article 169, the resolution of the Legislative Assembly seeking creation or abolition of a Legislative Council must be passed by:
o: A simple majority of members present and voting
A unanimous vote of all elected members
Two-thirds of the total membership of the Assembly
A majority of the total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting
accepted.x: The resolution requires a majority of the total membership of the Assembly and a majority of not less than two-thirds of members present and voting.
accepted.tq: Separate total-membership requirements from present-and-voting requirements.
accepted.sec: Article 169 - resolution majority, Parliament's role, Governor's role  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the law made by Parliament under Article 169:
1. Parliament passes the law by simple majority.
2. Such a law is deemed to be an amendment of the Constitution under Article 368.
3. Parliament determines the strength of the Legislative Council within the constitutional limits.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Parliament uses a simple majority and determines the Council's strength within the constitutional limits. The law is not deemed an amendment under Article 368, so statement 2 is false.
accepted.tq: Spot the constitutional-status trap in the statement that treats an ordinary law as an Article 368 amendment.
accepted.sec: Article 169 - resolution majority, Parliament's role, Governor's role  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the role of the Governor in the process under Article 169?
o: The Governor initiates the Assembly resolution for creation of the Council
The Governor alone can abolish the Legislative Council by notification
The Governor must approve the Assembly resolution before it is sent to Parliament
The Governor has no role in initiating or approving the resolution
accepted.x: The constitutional process is initiated by a special-majority resolution of the Legislative Assembly and completed through a law of Parliament; the Governor has no role in initiating or approving that resolution.
accepted.tq: Use the 'who would do this job?' test to reject powers wrongly assigned to the Governor.
accepted.sec: Article 169 - resolution majority, Parliament's role, Governor's role  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly explains the relationship between the State Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council under Article 169?
o: The Council can abolish itself by a simple majority resolution
The Council can permanently prevent the Assembly from seeking its abolition
The Governor decides whether the Council should continue
The existence of the Council depends on the will of the Assembly, subject to parliamentary action
accepted.x: The Assembly may pass the required special-majority resolution, after which Parliament may enact the law. Thus, the Council's existence depends on the will of the Assembly expressed through this constitutional process.
accepted.tq: Trace the complete institutional chain instead of assigning the final power to the wrong body.
accepted.sec: Article 169 - resolution majority, Parliament's role, Governor's role  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 168 — Officers of the State Legislature
Articles 178 to 187 — Presiding officers and related offices of the State Legislature
Articles 196 to 201 — Qualifications of members
Articles 202 to 207 — Judicial review of legislative proceedings
accepted.x: Articles 178 to 187 deal with the Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman, Deputy Chairman and related legislative offices. The other pairs assign unrelated subjects to those provisions.
accepted.tq: Use the range of articles as a structural clue and reject broad subject swaps.

accepted.s: The nominated representation in a State Legislative Council under Article 171 is:
o: One-fourth of its total membership
One-third of its total membership
One-sixth of its total membership
One-twelfth of its total membership
accepted.x: The Governor nominates one-sixth of the members of the Legislative Council from specified fields under Article 171.
accepted.tq: Test a constitutional fraction directly and distinguish it from the elected categories.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the Governor's addresses to the State Legislature is correct?
o: The Governor's address and special address are both optional
The Governor's special address is required at the first session after each general election and at the first session of each year
The Governor can address only the Legislative Council
The special address is required at the first session of every year
accepted.x: Article 176 provides for the Governor's special address at the first session after each general election and at the first session of each year.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the general power to address from the constitutionally required special occasions.

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct pairing of officers with the respective Houses of a bicameral State Legislature?
o: Speaker and Deputy Speaker — Legislative Assembly; Chairman and Deputy Chairman — Legislative Council
Chairman and Deputy Chairman — Legislative Assembly; Speaker and Deputy Speaker — Legislative Council
Speaker and Chairman — Legislative Assembly; Deputy Speaker and Deputy Chairman — Legislative Council
Governor and Speaker — Legislative Assembly; Chairman and Chief Minister — Legislative Council
accepted.x: The Assembly has a Speaker and Deputy Speaker, while the Council has a Chairman and Deputy Chairman.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the similar titles used for the two Houses.

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): The Speaker does not ordinarily vote in the first instance on a question before the Legislative Assembly.
Reason (R): The Speaker exercises a casting vote when there is an equality of votes.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true. The casting vote on a tie is a separate rule and does not explain why the Speaker abstains from voting in the first instance.
accepted.tq: Separate two related rules from a genuine cause-and-effect relationship.
accepted.sec: Speaker of the Legislative Assembly - powers, casting vote, Money Bill, resignation, vacating  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with the subject covered by the indicated Articles?
o: Articles 190–193 — Vacation of seats and disqualification
Articles 196–201 — Legislative procedure and assent
Article 194 — Powers and privileges
Article 210 — Creation and abolition of Legislative Councils
accepted.x: Article 210 concerns the language to be used in the State Legislature. Creation and abolition of Legislative Councils is dealt with under Article 169.
accepted.tq: Find the one article-range pair that belongs to a different constitutional subject.
